concept.name: Entry criterion
concept.definition: The explicit, predefined conditions that must all be present before a position is opened - the setup pattern, trigger, context filters, and confirmation requirements of the trading plan. Entry criteria turn good ideas into repeatable, testable decisions.
concept.intuition: The difference between a system and gambling is that the system can say 'not yet' in one sentence.
concept.mechanics: Defined per setup in the playbook - for example trend alignment, level, trigger bar or volume condition, and time window; a trade is taken only when every criterion is met and skipped otherwise. Documented criteria enable backtesting and post-trade grading of selection quality.
concept.failure_modes: Criteria that are vague admit impulse trades; criteria that are too numerous or curve-fitted to a small sample filter out nearly everything or break out of sample. Under FOMO, entry criteria are the first thing abandoned.
concept.misconceptions: A perfect entry is not the goal - sizing and exits matter more to expectancy; criteria exist for consistency, not precision. More confirmation is not always better: each added filter costs opportunity and can add fragility.
concept.example: Long only if: price above the rising 20-day average, the pullback holds the prior breakout level, and a reversal bar closes in its top third - all three required, every time.
